subject: System Design
title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Replication
description: A 60-second lesson on Synchronous vs Asynchronous Replication.

hook.text: Synchronous: the write waits for all replicas to confirm. Asynchronous: the write returns immediately.

buildup.text: Synchronous replication guarantees all replicas have the data but slows every write to the slowest replica.

discovery.text: Asynchronous replication is fast but risks data loss — if the primary dies before replication, writes are gone.

twist.text: Semi-synchronous is a middle ground: one replica must confirm synchronously, the rest catch up asynchronously.

climax.text: The choice between sync and async replication is a trade-off between durability and latency.

punchline.text: Sync is safe but slow. Async is fast but risky.

quiz.question: What is the risk of asynchronous replication?
options: Data loss if the primary fails before replicas receive writes
